claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

eu_status.description: The claimant's EU Settlement Scheme status, where relevant.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I need to ask you some questions.

First, do you have any children you're responsible for, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I have one child I'm asking about. My son Alex is 15 years old and lives with me here in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I have a few more questions to help determine your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Are you currently receiving Child Benefit for Alex, or is this a new claim you're considering making?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: This is a new claim I'm considering. I'm not currently receiving Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. To assess your eligibility, I need to understand a bit more about your situation.

Do you live in the UK, and if so, what is your immigration or residence status? For example, are you a UK citizen, do you have settled status, pre-settled status, or another type of status?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK. I have pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Since you have pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme, there are specific conditions you need to meet to be eligible for Child Benefit.

Are you currently working? If so, are you earning (or do you expect to earn) above the primary threshold for National Insurance contributions for at least 3 continuous months?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not sure about the exact National Insurance threshold details. Could you explain what that means or what the threshold is?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Of course, I'm happy to explain. The primary threshold for National Insurance contributions is the earnings level at which employees start paying National Insurance. For the current tax year (2024-25), this threshold is £242 per week, which works out to approximately £1,048 per month or £12,570 per year.

So the question is: Are you currently working and earning at least £242 per week (or about £1,048 per month) for at least 3 continuous months?

If you're not working, that's also fine to tell me - there are other ways you might qualify with pre-settled status, such as if you're looking for work, studying, or have sufficient resources to support yourself financially.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm honestly not sure about my financial situation in those terms. I don't know if I have sufficient resources or exactly how that's measured.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand - these terms can be unclear. Let me ask this more simply:

Are you currently:
1. Working in any job (employed or self-employed)?
2. Actively looking for work (registered as a jobseeker)?
3. Studying?
4. Or none of the above?

This will help me understand which category might apply to your situation.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'd rather not get into all those personal details right now. Can you just tell me - based on what I've told you so far about Alex being 15 and living with me - whether I'm eligible or not?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand your preference for privacy. Let me explain the situation based on what you've shared:

You've told me that:
- Alex is 15 years old and lives with you in the UK
- You have pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme

The challenge is that with pre-settled status, eligibility for Child Benefit depends on meeting specific additional conditions - such as being in work and earning above a certain threshold, being a jobseeker, being a student with sufficient resources, or having sufficient financial resources.

Without knowing which of these conditions applies to you, I cannot definitively determine whether you would be eligible or ineligible for Child Benefit. Your eligibility status is indeterminate based on the information available.

If you decide to apply, HMRC would assess whether you meet one of the qualifying conditions for someone with pre-settled status. Alternatively, if you're able to share whether any of those conditions apply to you, I could give you a more definitive answer.

Would you like me to provide my assessment based on what we've discussed, or would you prefer to share a bit more information?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, that's okay. I think I understand now - you're saying that because I have pre-settled status, there are extra requirements I'd need to meet, but without knowing more about my work or financial situation, you can't tell me for certain if I'm eligible. Is that right?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Yes, that's exactly right. You've understood it perfectly.

Because you have pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme, there are additional requirements beyond just having a child under 16 living with you in the UK. These extra requirements relate to your work status, financial resources, or other specific circumstances.

Without information about whether you meet one of those additional conditions, I cannot determine with certainty whether you would be eligible or ineligible for Child Benefit for Alex.

Since you've indicated you don't wish to share further details at this time, I'll record my assessment as indeterminate - meaning there isn't sufficient information to make a definitive eligibility determination.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I've recorded my assessment. Based on our conversation, your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex is **indeterminate** because while Alex meets the basic criteria (he's 15 and lives with you), the additional requirements for pre-settled status holders cannot be assessed without more information about your circumstances.

If you decide to gather more details about your work or financial situation and would like to discuss this further in the future, please feel free to come back. You could also contact HMRC directly to discuss your specific situation - they can assess your full circumstances when you apply.
